## Intent
Define a better, GENERIC way to handle gaps in old (terminal) intents, and stop shipping one user's store into everyone's package. Two coupled problems. (1) Owner rejected the frozen-allowlist approach to the signals_complete gaps (44 today in the owner store: ~40 missing outcome.md, 3 missing the savepoint Done echo, 1 placeholder): an id allowlist defines fixes for ONE store, not for all users, and it does not scale. (2) VERIFIED 2026-07-16 this is not hypothetical: scripts/lib/legacy_bookend_amnesty.rb (intent 170a) ALREADY ships in the npm package - scripts/ is in package.json files and npm pack --dry-run packs it - hardcoding the OWNER's personal intent ids (global 1a/1a2/23 and ~70 project:plastic ids), so every Plastic installer worldwide receives one user's intent numbers baked into shipped maintenance code. Plastic must instead define the BARE MINIMUM set of generic fixes that apply to ALL users as RULES not id lists (e.g. a predicate keyed on 'terminal before feature X existed' or 'operational file missing', evaluated against each user's own store at runtime, never a shipped snapshot of ids). Constrained by owner rulings 2026-07-16 carried in 197: stay away from backfilling DONE intents; only fix a Done intent when it is missing something OPERATIONAL (a core file so the intent cannot be read/processed), never for a cosmetic or delivery-claim gap; a missing outcome.md is a delivery CLAIM maintenance must never invent; any batch touching many intents needs owner approval with the diff shown first. Deliverable: a design for generic old-intent gap handling (what is operational vs cosmetic, how the minimum-fix predicate is expressed and run per-store at runtime, what doctor should report vs suppress without an id list), plus removing/replacing the shipped store-specific amnesty file. Leave the 44 alone until this lands. Spun out of 197 (the maintenance-vs-work ruling); the amnesty precedent traces to 170a.

## Context
(why this intent exists — background, then ### Decisions after brainstorming)

Update from intent 197 (2026-07-17, delivered on branch plastic/197, not yet merged): 197 shipped the WORK vs MAINTENANCE separation, the maintenance tooling (MaintenanceGit, maintenance-run, RevisionsWriter receipt-before-write, the curator refuse-without-receipt contract, end-intent scoped commit, doctor fix_hint routing) and repaired the three live graph_links_projection violations (global 26, dealintell 3b, dealintell 15/3a) through that tooling with append-only receipts. Still 211's scope, deliberately untouched by 197 (verified in 197's ACTION_13 non-goals gate): the 44 signals_complete terminal gaps (40 missing outcome.md, 3 missing the Done echo, 1 placeholder), removing scripts/lib/legacy_bookend_amnesty.rb (it ships hardcoded owner intent ids, the anti-pattern), and the founding rule that no personal or user-specific store data ever ships in the package.

Discovery deposited 2026-07-19 (resources/discovery--legacy-gap-predicate.md, HEAD 7615108): confirmed the amnesty file's exact shape (a frozen `{scope => [ids]}` hash, 3 global + 60 project:plastic ids), every reader (doctor.rb's require/constant/constructor seam, phantom-line suppression, Done-echo suppression, installer_core.rb's core_files registration), that no other code path reads it, and that npm pack --dry-run still packs it today. Pulled 219's spec.md D6 verbatim (done work is immutable; outcome.md absence is never fabricated; savepoint.md absence may be minimally reconstructed) and 219's Slice Boundary Map row naming 211's exact territory (the generic predicate applied through savepoint_truthful/stalled_completion, plus amnesty removal). Confirmed the two already-shipped Bridge primitives (rebuild_savepoint, append_terminal_savepoint) compose into the 124a two-line reconstruction recipe with zero new mechanical code needed, and that maintenance-run has no fourth --tool slot for it yet. Confirmed via a full-tree grep of every .freeze'd array/hash literal in scripts/ that zero legitimate exemptions are needed for a packaging guard keyed on 5+ Folgezettel-shaped tokens in one literal.

### Decisions
- D1: The generic predicate is a repairability classification computed at runtime from file presence alone (no injected or shipped id list): a missing/placeholder outcome.md on a terminal intent is a delivery-claim gap (unrepairable, per 219 D6); a missing savepoint.md entirely (a case not previously checked at all) or one missing the Done delivered|abandoned line is an operational gap (repairable). Non-terminal-intent gaps are untouched (222's close gate owns that surface).
- D2: `signals_complete` is repurposed to the outcome-only bucket and its severity flips from warn to always pass (matching check_skill_lint's existing advisory precedent: count + details in the message, no fix_hint/fixable, since fabricating outcome.md is never a legitimate fix). A NEW check, `savepoint_operational`, takes the operational bucket (missing savepoint.md or missing Done echo): warn, fixable, fix_hint routes to `maintenance-run --tool rebuild-savepoint --intent <id> --apply`. `savepoint_truthful` keeps its name and warn-only severity (134's advisory ruling intact) but drops id-based suppression outright: every terminal phantom line is now always advisory, never suppressed, since the message already labeled it report-only. `stalled_completion` and `signals_agree` are unchanged (neither ever read `@bookend_amnesty`).
- D3: `scripts/lib/legacy_bookend_amnesty.rb` is deleted along with every reader: doctor.rb's require, the LEGACY_BOOKEND_AMNESTY constant, and the constructor's `bookend_amnesty:` parameter/`@bookend_amnesty` ivar (no DI seam survives); installer_core.rb's core_files registration entry is deleted. The already-installed copy needs no separate migration: the existing `old_files - new_files` manifest diff in installer_core.rb (verified generic, two call sites) prunes it on the next install/update.
- D4: The packaging guard proving the founding hard rule is a new Minitest file (`test/packaging_no_store_ids_test.rb`), not a doctor check (219's three scopes diagnose an installed tree, not the distributable itself; this matches install_packaging_test.rb's existing precedent). It derives the shipped-file set from package.json's own "files" array (never a hand list) and scans for a `%w[]`/bracket-of-quoted-strings literal carrying 5+ Folgezettel-shaped tokens (`\A\d+[a-zA-Z0-9]*\z`). Proven via a fixture (RED, independent of whether the real file still exists) plus a real-shipped-tree scan (GREEN, post-removal: this is the actual proof case, since it would have failed against pre-removal main). A full-tree audit found zero legitimate exemptions needed at the 5-token threshold.
- D5: `maintenance-run` gains a fourth tool, `rebuild-savepoint --intent <id>`, matching the existing three tools' exact shape (single-intent, lock-checked via check_not_fresh!, dry-run default, MaintenanceGit.run_scoped + RevisionsWriter.append! receipt). It composes Bridge.rebuild_savepoint + Bridge.append_terminal_savepoint with the disposition read only from outcome.md's frontmatter (124a precedent, never invented); it refuses loudly if outcome.md is missing or a placeholder. Batch application against the owner's 44 live gaps is explicitly NOT run by this intent (owner-approval-gated per 197): this intent wires the tool only.
- D6: Five DI-based tests in test/doctor_done_signals_test.rb referencing `bookend_amnesty:` (plus two whose premise, allowlist grandfathering, no longer exists) are rewritten/deleted to assert the new check shapes directly, with one new fixture added for the previously-uncovered "savepoint.md missing entirely" case. No injected suppression parameter survives anywhere in the test file.

- [[197--separate-maintenance-from-work|Separate maintenance from work: work is immutable, maintenance is not (owner ruling 2026-07-14). What an intent DELIVERED (intent text, spec, plan, outcome) is frozen once terminal and must never be edited so the intent looks like it delivered something else. But MAINTENANCE (structural consistency: closing an intent, making structure uniform across stores, reprojecting Links, moving a section where it belongs) is explicitly allowed on terminal intents, on one condition: every fix is recorded in the intent's revisions.md and runs through a Plastic maintenance skill, never a hand edit. PLASTIC.md must state the distinction plainly so no agent confuses the two, because today's blanket terminal-immutability rule DEADLOCKS the store: a real structural defect cannot be repaired for the sole reason that the intent is Completed, which is exactly how the three graph_links_projection violations (global 26, dealintell 3b, dealintell 15) survived the two intents built to fix them (189, 192 both closed with the repair PROPOSED, not run). - [[219--doctor-check-surface-doctrine|GOVERNING intent, owner rulings 2026-07-19: define the doctor check-surface doctrine so doctor tells us Plastic is properly INSTALLED and properly USED as releases add features and deprecations. Three scopes, strictly separated. (1) core check: very fast, binary, operational-only - Plastic is loaded and ready for work on every registered agent (currently Claude Code and Codex): skills, subagents, hooks/harnesses present and lazy-loaded so they cost just enough context for an agent to lead delivery through Plastic; every registered project has a store on disk with its repository/directory pointed at, and the global store is available; nothing else. On core failure the user gets a guided route: plastic doctor --fix, if that fails roll back to the last working version restored from backups, and report the issue via a feedback command if the user wants. (2) store scan: also fast - verify the operations Plastic itself depends on work in that one store: QMD search over intents, sources/chain resolution, everything that sets context. (3) full project check: runs when the project is loaded, NOT before, and its findings stay scoped to that project - never reported globally with the core check (today's pain). The thorough store check exists to keep every store the SAME STRUCTURE: the same artifacts delivered by the same intent-driven process, so work is easily scoped and what was promised is verifiable against what was delivered. Systems never lie: done work is immutable (you cannot rewrite the moment you drilled the wrong hole in the wall for the TV; the past changes only through new intent delivery). Terminal work therefore stays as-is unless something OPERATIONAL to today's Plastic is missing: a missing outcome.md can NEVER be inferred or fabricated, but a missing savepoint.md MAY be reconstructed minimally (even two lines, started and Done, signifying checked and done) - this ruling enriches 211's generic operational-missing-vs-cosmetic predicate and 211 consumes it at its Why. Artifact completeness checking moves to the intent-end phase as a scripted per-intent check (spawned slice). Config honoring is part of the mandate: after install/update completes, user modifications to config (per-agent model choices, e.g. Opus vs Fable advisor, GPT 5.5 vs 5.6) must be honored - already in flight via the agent-model drift checks (184/186/216), kept as non-boot doctor checks. Spawns the core-check rescope, the store-scan/load-time scoping, and the intent-end structure check on its chain; relates to 208 (falsifiable checks), 209 (pass-by-construction audit), 204, 184, 216, and delivered 197 (doctor stays a detector; Fix-all is a router).]]
